ruleName: Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions (Including Immovable Obstructions)
title: How far from the nearest point of complete relief may you drop your ball from a cart path?
question: Your ball is on a cart path. You are entitled to free relief. How far from the nearest point of complete relief may you drop your ball?

choices.text: As far as you like, provided it is no nearer the hole.

explanation: When taking free relief from a cart path, the ball must be dropped within one club-length of the nearest point of complete relief, not nearer the hole, as specified under Rule 16.1b.

juniorVersion.title: How far can you drop your ball from the cart path?
juniorVersion.question: Your ball is on a cart path. You get to move it without a penalty. How far away from where you get complete relief can you drop your ball?

choices.text: As far as you want, as long as it is not closer to the hole.

juniorVersion.explanation: When your ball is on a cart path, you must drop it within one club-length from the nearest spot where you are not touching the path, your feet and ball are both off the path, and you are not closer to the hole.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A hard road on the golf course where buggies or golf carts drive.
Moving your ball to get away from something on the course, like a puddle or a path, without a penalty.
The closest spot where you can stand and the ball can be without touching the path or thing you are moving from.
The distance from one end of your club to the other, used to measure how far you can drop the ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show them how to use their own club to measure the dropping area. Remind them that they can't go closer to the hole.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can move the ball as far as you want.
Dropping farther away than one club-length.
Forgetting to measure with your own club.
